messages.subject: Using normalize with priors in model
messages.subject_clean: Using normalize with priors in model
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am interested in using the TMB::normalize() function to calculate the GMRF normalizing constant due to computational constraints. However, I am running into issues when I also specify priors for other parameters in the model. It appears that priors are being disregarded as I get the same results no matter what priors I choose.

I have attached a small example (normalize_example.R) that compares using TMB::normalize() with GMRF(Q, false) and only using GMRF(Q) under several different prior scenarios. When using TMB::normalize() with GMRF(Q, false), I get the exact same results regardless of the priors. When I use only GMRF(Q) I get different results each time, which is what I would expect to happen. As an additional note, the results from both methods match exactly if I remove the priors altogether.

This is the model I am fitting:

// Data likelihood
y_i | p_i ~ Binomial(n_i, p_i)
logit(p_i) = alpha + A_i^T * S // A_i is a vector that maps S from mesh points to location i

// Random effects
S | logtau, logkappa ~ N(0, Q^{-1}(logtau, logkappa))

// Priors
alpha ~ N(alphamean, 1)
logtau ~ N(logtaumean, 1)
logkappa ~ N(logkappamean, 1)

where I try different values of alphamean, logtaumean, and logkappamean.

If anyone has insight/recommendations on this issue, I would greatly appreciate it.

Thank you!
Katie

messages.body_plain:
Should work if you regard hyper priors as part of the 'data likelihood', i.e. change to something like:

// Hyperpriors
if (flag != 0)  nll -= dnorm(logtau, logtaumean , Type(1.0), true);
if (flag != 0)  nll -= dnorm(logkappa, logkappamean , Type(1.0), true);

Or alternatively, move the hyper priors to after 'if (flag == 0) return nll;'.

Please verify that this is correct and report back, thanks! (I need to add it to the documentation)

Though, I did find that the values of the parameters after running the optimizer are the same between the 2 approaches. I'm attaching an updated version of the code that includes this extra random effect in the model.

I have also tried several different combinations of moving contributions to nll to before/after the flag with no success.

messages.subject: Suppressing warning from dyn.unload()
messages.body_plain:
Hi TMBers

I have a closed loop sim project that I'm working on, and I like to unload the TMB libraries between time steps and replicates, since I'm occasionally switching TMB estimation models and don't want to have a conflict. However, I don't love the repetitive warnings:

Warning: 3 external pointers will be removed

Warning: 5 external pointers will be removed

Warning: 3 external pointers will be removed

Warning: 5 external pointers will be removed

Warning: 3 external pointers will be removed

I've tried using

suppressWarnings(dyn.unload(dynlib("assessDD")))

and setting options(warn = -1) during the execution of the commands, but to no avail.

Does anyone have any experience with this?

Thanks
Sam

messages.subject: Re: Suppressing warning from dyn.unload()
messages.body_plain:
The warning says you're about to unload the code needed to free those pointers. Maybe you could clean up before unloading:

rm(obj); gc()
dyn.unload(...)
